title: Interactive admin REPL + runbook validation harness
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary:
We will build an interactive admin REPL (read-eval-print loop) that lets oncall engineers execute runbook-as-task workflows against a sandboxed control plane, inspect intermediate state (KV cache, routing decisions, active batches), and optionally escalate to live execution. Alongside the REPL, implement a runbook validation harness that can execute runbook steps against deterministic mocks and synthetic infra to detect brittle steps, missing fallbacks, and side-effecting commands before they reach production runbooks.

Why:
- Current runbook changes are hard to validate without running in prod; bugs lead to truncated rollouts and pager noise.
- Engineers need a fast feedback loop for operational playbooks (esp. autoscaling, failover, capacity routing).
- A REPL reduces time to diagnose by surfacing runtime primitives (routing policy, cache hits/misses, kernel selections) and allowing replaying a request path.

Scope / Non-goals:
- Scope: REPL UI + CLI prototype, sandboxed executor, runbook validator harness, basic telemetry and audit logging, integration with existing runbook templates. Include guardrails for KMS/HSM access and push approval flows.
- Non-goal: full RBAC migration or on-prem packaging for this sprint.

Deliverables:
1) repl-cli binary (alpha) that connects to a sandbox control plane endpoint.
2) web-based REPL pane in Console (read-only for alpha) for inspectors.
3) runbook-validator service that runs steps against mocks and outputs a pass/fail plus explanation.
4) telemetry dashboard for validation runs and REPL usage metrics.
5) docs: quickstart, security checklist, and a set of 5 canonical validation tests for common failure modes.
acceptance_criteria: REPL CLI can authenticate with sandbox and run a stored runbook in dry-run mode
Runbook validator executes each step against mocks and reports deterministic status and diffed side-effects
All REPL actions are audited and visible in Console logs within 15 minutes
Telemetry shows REPL usage and validator pass rates in the ops dashboard
Security sweep performed and documented; KMS access denied in sandbox by default
